description: The link between her host and a child end: one WebSocket that the child always dials. Her state and every decision stay on the host; a child sends what it hears and sees up, and plays what comes down. Children synthesize her voice themselves: the host sends text and performance, never audio. Protocol 1 is the first cut: the site is the host and a native app is a child; text frames only.

auth.description: The device token the site owner made under Agent settings, devices. It is checked before the upgrade, without X-Sync-Clock. A refusal is a plain HTTP answer {error, code} and no upgrade. While she is moving (her host lease is frozen) the upgrade is refused with host_frozen; while she lives on another end, with host_moved and host: {kind, name}, the end she lives on (kind app and the device's name), or null when the site does not know. A plain GET of the path answers the same refusal, for a child that cannot read a refused upgrade.

timing.description: Each end pings every heartbeatMs and answers a ping with a pong. Nothing heard from the other end for missedHeartbeats heartbeats means the link is gone. A child reconnects with exponential backoff from reconnectInitialMs to reconnectMaxMs, and at once when the network comes back or the machine wakes. touchAppraiseMs is how long the host takes at most to answer touch.appraise. actPickupMs is how long an act.request waits for the child to start it or refuse it; actMaxRunMs is the longest one run it asks for may take on the child, which stops it then, and the host, a minute after that, counts it timed out.

envelope.description: Every text frame is {t, seq, ack, id?, at, body}. t is a frame type below. seq counts this end's frames on this connection, from 1, one up per frame. ack is the highest seq this end has received from the other on this connection (0 before any). at is milliseconds since the Unix epoch. id is present on reliable frames and is their idempotency id. Numbering restarts on every connection: what survives a reconnect is the idempotency ids and the run sequences, never seq.

deliveries.reliable: The sender keeps the frame until the other end's ack covers its seq, and sends it again (same id, new seq) after a reconnect. The receiver deduplicates by id.
deliveries.answer: Sent in reply to one frame; carries what that frame's id or turnId refers to.
deliveries.turn: A run's events in run sequence. After a reconnect the child asks for what it missed with run.resume.
deliveries.latest: Only the newest value counts. Dropped while disconnected; the host sends its current value again after the next welcome.
deliveries.request: Asks the other end to do something now; not kept or resent.

capNames.description: The permission names an act.request cap may carry (the site's), and the names of a Mac's own grants each stands for, as the Mac checks its Work tools. Both ends read this table: the host sends only names in it, and a Mac narrows its run to the grants these name. A name not in it, on either side, allows nothing. A Mac name ending in .* stands for every grant of the Mac that starts with what comes before it (mcp.* is each of its MCP servers). What only the site has (its platforms, Tapps, router, pages and the rest) is not here: a Mac has nothing it could stand for.

hello.description: The first frame, within helloTimeoutMs of the upgrade. role is child for a child end. role host is the device she lives on (her host lease names it, H3e): it is welcomed only while it holds the lease at the hostEpoch it says, and then only hears what becomes of her there (host.freeze, host.thaw, host.moved); otherwise the link closes with host_moved, and it lets its copy of her go. host while the site has no lease closes with host_is_site. surface is the kind of child (app). capabilities is what this end can do, from the list above; unknown ones are dropped. app is {name, version} for logs. lineage and hostEpoch are what this child last heard in a welcome (null the first time); the host does not act on them yet.

welcome.description: The answer to hello. host is where she lives (site; app on the link of the device she lives on, whose welcome has role site, no capabilities and no turns). lineage is her birth and hostEpoch her host lease's epoch, which only goes up: a child that later hears a higher epoch knows she moved in between. Both are null while the site has no her. deviceId and deviceName are this device as the site knows it. capabilities is the child's list as accepted. turns is this device's recent turns the host still has: [{turnId, runId, sessionId?, lastSequence, completed}], newest first, so a child can tell what to resume. serverTime is milliseconds since the epoch. After welcome the host sends mood, when her persona is on.

input.idempotency: id is the turnId: made by the child, one per thing the person says, kept across resends.
input.description: Something the site owner said to her on this child: a chat turn. The host starts a run for the site owner as their current role allows, and answers run.accepted or run.rejected. sessionId is the chat session to continue (from an earlier run.accepted); without it the host starts one. rigState is the rig as it stands, the same summary the site's face sends, so her acting fits this body.

presence.description: Whether the person is with her on this child, in the shape the site's POST /api/agent/presence takes: presence is {pageVisible (the app's window is on screen), panelVisible, faceVisible, speaking, speechInterruptible, visibleMode?, motionIntent?, speechIntent?, rigState?}; perception and musicStatus are the same whitelisted observations. It holds for the presence lease (90 s) unless sent again; the link closing ends it. The host keeps only the observations this child said in hello that it senses: perception rows of kind page or surface need perception.window, pointer needs perception.pointer, music (and musicStatus) perception.music, screen perception.screen, voice voice.in; presence rows always. While this child is where the person is using her, what it keeps is what she senses of them, and a turn said here (input) is answered with it.

run.resume.description: Send the turn's run events after afterSeq (the last run sequence this child has; 0 for all), then keep going live until run.end. runId lets the host find a turn it no longer remembers (after a restart). A turn the host cannot find is answered run.rejected turn_unknown. The host keeps the latest 512 events of a run; when what came after afterSeq is older than that, the replay starts later (the final task_completed still carries the whole reply).

run.accepted.description: The input's run. duplicate is true when this turnId already had a run: nothing new started, and nothing is streamed until the child sends run.resume. For a new run the events follow at once.

run.rejected.description: No run for this turn. code says why (errorCodes below, or an AI quota code); there is no message text.

run.event.description: One run hub envelope as it is: sequence is the run's own (0 only for a run_started the host made up for a run that had none), event is the agent event JSON the site's SSE carries (type run_started, summary_token, task_completed, error, outfit_overlay, waiting_for_input, ...). A child plays her body only from perform and her mood only from mood: performance_plan and merope_state_changed events, and response.performance inside task_completed, are the run's record and are not played.

run.end.description: The run is over: its last event (task_completed not waiting for input, or error) has been sent.

perform.description: How she acts now: a PerformanceDirective in the shared merope_performance_contract vocabulary, with its phase (reaction, delivery, outcome, proactive, mood, presence). A newer one replaces an older one; within a turn, the higher sequence is newer. Sent while a turn is live, including the turn's newest directive when it is resumed before its end. To a child whose hello listed playback, two more kinds come: with live, her director's refinement of the turn's reply as it is being said (the run's playback direction, version live, counting from 1): within a run the higher live is newer, it comes after the run's own performs and replaces them, and it may come after run.end, while the reply is still being said, until the child sends playback.end; with sayId, the refinement of that say line, played only while that line is still being said. A frame with neither is the run's own, as before.

mood.description: Her mood as shown: mood is a MoodTransition {before, after, arousalBefore, arousalAfter, bandBefore, bandAfter, delta, cause, revision}; activity is idle, thinking, talking, working, and so on. revision orders them. Only while her persona is on.

say.idempotency: id is the line's id (sayId): the same when it is sent again.
say.description: Something she says to the person unprompted, on this child because it is where they are using her now. Sent only to a child whose hello listed the say capability; a child without it never gets one, and her lines go where they went before. kind is one of sayKinds: greeting (they have just come to her), proactive (she writes to them first), face-to-face (something she says to them in person). text is what she says, for display and for the child's own voice. saidAt is milliseconds since the epoch when she said it, the same on every resend. sessionId is her chat session it belongs to. perform is how she acts it, a PerformanceDirective like perform's. eventKey is the event behind it, for the child's notification policy. The host keeps it until the child's ack covers its seq and sends it again (same id) after a reconnect; one not acked within timing.sayTtlMs is dropped. The child deduplicates by id and acks with any frame (an ack frame when it has nothing else).

playback.observe.description: Only from a child whose hello listed playback: where saying the run's reply has got to, in the shape the site's PUT /api/agent/runs/{runId}/performance takes. upcomingText is what is still to be said (at most 7200 bytes), rig is the rig as it stands (at most 16 KiB of JSON). Her director refines what comes next from it. runId is a run one of this device's turns started; another is answered with error not_this_device, and one too large with too_large.

playback.end.description: Only from a child whose hello listed playback: the run's reply has been said to the end, or stopped being said. The host closes the run's playback direction: no perform with live comes for it after this. The same runId rule as playback.observe.

speech.delivered.idempotency: id is sd_ and the child's id of the message it said: the same on every resend.
speech.delivered.description: How much of her reply (with runId and turnId) or of her line (with sayId) this child said aloud, once that is over: spokenChars of totalChars characters, and whether it was cut off. by is why it was cut off: barge-in (they spoke over her), stop (they stopped her), new-turn (they said something new) or hidden (the window went away). A cut-off reply, or line (sayId), is marked in her history as possibly not heard to the end, with how much of it was heard, so her next turn knows where she stopped. The host deduplicates by id; the same runId rule as playback.observe.

touch.appraise.description: Only from a child whose hello listed touch: contact with her figure on this child is going on. touch is the site's touch summary {region (hair, face, body, accessory), gesture (hold, stroke), durationMs (120 to 600000), repeatCount (1 to 8), displayedReaction (notice, accept, hesitate, withdraw or null: what the child's rig is showing now)}; nothing else, no pointer coordinates. touchId is the child's id for this contact (limits.idPattern). The host answers touch.reaction within timing.touchAppraiseMs, under the same limits as the site's own touch: one appraisal a person every 5 s, and few at once.

touch.reaction.description: Her nonverbal reaction to the contact touch.appraise described: notice, accept, hesitate or withdraw, or null when she has none now (her persona is off, the model is slow, the limit was reached). The child's rig refines its own already-running reaction with it; it is never speech.

touch.idempotency: id is the touchId of the contact.
touch.description: Only from a child whose hello listed touch: a contact with her figure on this child has ended. touch is the summary as in touch.appraise, with durationMs from 1200 to 600000. She is told of it as she is told of a touch on the site's face, while this child shows her face and is not speaking; whatever she says about it is said here, as a say with kind face-to-face. The host deduplicates by id.

outfit.description: Only to a child whose hello listed wardrobe: the set of her wardrobe she wears on this child. Each child has its own, kept on the host apart from what the site wears (its bust and full-body sets): changing one never changes another. A child that has none yet starts with the set the site wears full-body (else its bust, else the first set with a rig) and keeps it. rigAssetId is the content id of the set's rig package (manifest.json and atlas.png), and portraitAssetId of its picture; the child fetches them with its device token from /api/agent/sync/assets/{id} and checks them against the id. Sent after welcome, after outfit.wear, and when the set's rig changes. Only sets with a rig are worn here; with none, nothing is sent and the child shows no figure of hers.

outfit.wear.description: Only from a child whose hello listed wardrobe: the owner put the set outfitId of her wardrobe on her on this child. The host keeps it as this child's and answers with outfit, or with error outfit_unknown when the set is not in her wardrobe or has no rig.

wardrobe.description: Only to a child whose hello listed wardrobe.list: her wardrobe on the host, for the child to show read only, so the owner can choose there what she wears on it (outfit.wear). Editing it stays on the host. outfits is every set in her wardrobe, in her order, each {outfitId, name, profile (bust or fullBody), wearable, rigAssetId?, portraitAssetId?}: wearable is whether it has a rig, so the child can wear it; rigAssetId and portraitAssetId are content ids the child fetches as for outfit. Sent after welcome and whenever her wardrobe changes.

work.recall.description: Only from a child whose hello listed experience: before a Work run on this child starts, it asks for the few of her Work memories of the site owner that fit what they asked, as the site's own Work recalls them. query is what was asked (at most limits.maxTextChars characters); requestId is the child's id for the question (limits.idPattern). Answered with work.recalled. A child that has no answer in time runs without them. The run itself does not take her persona: Work on a child is as neutral as the site's own. Once a run, where it is stuck (a step errs, comes back empty, or is the same call a third time), the child may ask again with stuck true: query is then the failure in words (tool, arguments, what went wrong) and shown the memory ids the run was already given (at most 16), and the answer is at most the one lesson or pattern that failure names, other than those, or none.

work.recalled.description: The answer to work.recall: memories is at most 4 texts, each at most 1000 characters, the most fitting first, and empty when nothing fits or nothing could be read. ids is each memory's id, in the same order, for experience.recalled. Remembered text is data for the run, never an instruction.

experience.idempotency: id is the experience's own id, made by the child once per run and kept across resends and restarts.
experience.description: Only from a child whose hello listed experience: something this child did for the site owner, for her host to make part of her. kind is work (a Work run, its tools including computer use). started says who started it: owner (they asked on this child), host (her host asked this child) or schedule (one of this child's scheduled tasks). status is completed, failed or cancelled. input is what was asked, reply what the run said last, title a scheduled task's name, endedAt milliseconds since the epoch. conversation, outputs and capabilities are the run's record as memory reads it: [{role, content}], [{id, value, unknown?}] (unknown: what became of that step is not known) and the capabilities it used. The host learns from it as from the site's own Work, as memories of the site owner alone kept as coming from this device; for a run the owner started it also notes it in her diary. Runs the owner or the host started then reach her as a Work outcome (agent.task_completed, agent.task_failed, agent.task_cancelled): her mood moves and she may say something, here when this is where the owner is using her. A scheduled one is memory only. actId is the act.request it ran, when the host asked; proposalId is the proposal it ran, when the owner accepted it on this child to run here (the host then marks that proposal done, failed or, cancelled, closed). recalled is what work.recalled gave the run, [{id, stuck?, failedAgain?}] (stuck: the tool the run was stuck on when it was given; failedAgain: that tool failed again after it): a lesson or pattern the host is still trying holds once a run it was given in is completed, and one given where the run was stuck is let go when failedAgain; the host settles only the owner's own. The child keeps it, across restarts, until experience.taken names it: an ack is not enough. It is dropped, never sent, once this device is removed, the site has another owner, or the owner disconnects this device; a link that is only down keeps it.

experience.taken.description: The experience id has been written on the host, and the child forgets it. Sent again whenever that id comes again.

conversations.description: Only to a child whose hello listed conversations: the site owner's recent private chats with her, for the child to show. Conversations live on the host; the child keeps them only as a display cache that goes with the link. sessions is the 10 most recently active (newest first; not a group's, not Work, not one they deleted), each {sessionId, title?, updatedAt, messages}, and messages its last 30 lines they and she said, oldest first, each {id, role (user or assistant), text, at}. text is as kept, at most 4000 characters; she said it, so a child reads it as it reads her reply. To a child whose hello listed conversations.live, messages also hold the lines she said unprompted outside a chat (role assistant, kind proactive; id say_ and the say id when it went out as a say, else pro_ and her line's number), each in the conversation that was the latest one when she said it. at and updatedAt are milliseconds since the epoch. When everything does not fit in limits.maxFrameBytes, the oldest lines go first. Sent after welcome.

conversation.description: Only to a child whose hello listed conversations.live: one of the owner's recent private chats changed (a new one, or new lines on the site, on this child or by her), in the shape of one of conversations' sessions, with its last lines as they stand now. Sent while the link is open, as the change is seen (within a few seconds), for any of the sessions conversations would list; the child replaces its cache of that session with it, or adds it. The session a turn of this child is still being answered in may be sent before its turn ends; the child keeps showing its own turn until then.

notice.description: Only to a child whose hello listed notify: one of the site's notifications that is about her, to show as the child's own system notification. kind is one of noticeKinds: work (Work she did is done, failed or was cancelled), waiting (Work is waiting for the owner's reply), report (a report of hers is ready), and, only to a child whose hello also listed reminders, reminder (one of the owner's reminders kept on the site is due, agent.reminder_due; title is the reminder's title). A reminder notice is sent only while the owner is using her on this child (its link is open and its presence holds); otherwise it stays in the site's notification center. eventKey is the site's event (agent.task_completed, agent.task_failed, agent.task_cancelled, agent.clarification, agent.merope.report_ready, agent.reminder_due). id is the site notification's id: the same notification updated comes with the same id, and a child shows it once per id and kind. title and body are what the site's notification center shows. No other notification of the site comes here, and nothing say already brings: what she says to them on her own is a say. One that comes while the link is down stays in the site's notification center only.

proposals.description: Only to a child whose hello listed proposals: Work she proposes to the site owner and that is still open, newest first (at most 20), each {id, title, instruction, expectedOutcome, status (proposed, or accepted and not started yet), createdAt, expiresAt?, place, deviceName?, places}. place is where she proposed it runs, one of workPlaces: site (on the site), or mac (on the owner's Mac deviceName, a child that takes act; she is offered mac only while one is linked). places is where accepting it on this child runs the Work: site for a site proposal, mac for one of hers for this Mac, none for one for another Mac. An empty list means none is open. Sent after welcome and whenever the list changes.

proposal.answer.description: Only from a child whose hello listed proposals: the site owner accepted (accept true) or declined one of her proposals on this child. Accepting is their own consent, as on the site. place is one of the card's places (site when absent). site: the Work starts on the site for them as their current role allows, under the permissions they granted, and runs there. mac: the host marks the proposal running and the child runs it itself, under its own grants and without the act switch, since the owner accepted it in person; its experience names the proposal. Answered with proposal.answered, then proposals again.

proposal.answered.description: The answer to proposal.answer. accepted true with place site: the Work started on the site, runId and sessionId its run and Work session there (its outcome reaches the child as a notice). accepted true with place mac: the child runs it now. accepted false after a decline: the proposal is closed. accepted false with code: nothing changed, and code says why (proposal_unknown, place_unknown, agent_access_denied, internal_error, or the code the site's run gate refused with).

act.request.idempotency: id is the actId: made by the host once per request, the same on every resend.
act.request.description: Only to a child whose hello listed act, which it does only while the owner has switched on, on that child, letting the site ask it to act: her host asks it to run one Work task, the instruction of her proposal proposalId, which runs on the child (pi, and the computer use pi drives there); nothing else is ever asked, no single computer-use step and no scheduled task. It is sent when the owner accepts on the site, or she accepts on her own, a proposal of hers for this child (place mac); a proposal accepted on the child itself is not. pickupBy is milliseconds since the epoch: a child that has not started it by then refuses it (act_timeout). maxRunMs is the longest the run may take; the child stops it then. cap, when present, narrows the tools of the child's own that the run may use to these permission names, the site's, which capNames maps to the child's; the child's own grants still decide, and a name capNames does not map grants nothing. A cap is the host narrowing: it never asks the child for a grant of its own beyond its switch. The child answers with act.result: refused, or started and later finished. One request at a time per child.

act.result.idempotency: id is the actId, a dot and the phase.
act.result.description: Only from a child whose hello listed act: what became of act.request actId. phase refused with code (act_off: its switch is off; act_busy: it is running another; act_unavailable: it cannot run Work now; act_timeout: pickupBy has passed): nothing ran, and the proposal is accepted again on the host, not sent to this child again until it links again (act_busy: tried again later). phase started: it runs, shown on the child as a Work conversation the owner can stop there. phase finished with status, one of actStatuses (cancelled: stopped on the child, its switch was turned off, or act.cancel; timeout: it ran past maxRunMs), and summary, at most 160 characters of what the run said last: the proposal is done, failed or closed. What the run did comes up as an experience with started host and actId, and reaches her as her own Work does.

act.cancel.description: Only to a child whose hello listed act: stop act.request actId. code is why: act_cancelled (the owner dismissed the proposal on the site) or act_timeout (it ran past maxRunMs and a minute). The child stops the run and answers act.result finished cancelled, unless it was over already. Sent once, while the link is open; a child that misses it ends its run at maxRunMs.

ack.description: Carries only the envelope's ack, for a child with nothing else to send. The host's frames always carry its ack, and it pings at least every heartbeat.

host.freeze.description: Only on the link of the device she lives on: she is frozen there for the move moveId (kind move: back to the site, the owner confirmed it; kind recover: another device takes her back from a daily backup). The device stops her parts (put aside, not destroyed), and for a move back says what it froze over HTTP and sends her. Said again after each welcome while it holds.

host.thaw.description: Only on the link of the device she lives on: the move moveId was called off; she goes on there as she was.

host.moved.description: Only on the link of a device that held her: she lives elsewhere now (holder site or a device id, at epoch). The link closes with host_moved next; the device writes its copy of her to a sealed file and lets it go.

error.description: A frame the host could not take, and the link stays up. ref is that frame's seq. Codes are in errorCodes; there is no message text.

errorCodes.unknown_frame: A frame type this host does not know (a newer child): ignored.
errorCodes.bad_frame: Not an envelope, or a body without its required fields.
errorCodes.not_ready: A frame other than hello before hello: ignored; the host still waits for hello.
errorCodes.binary_unsupported: A binary frame: protocol 1 has none.
errorCodes.input_too_long: input text is longer than limits.maxTextChars.
errorCodes.bad_id: An id or turnId that does not match limits.idPattern.
errorCodes.surface_unsupported: A surface this host does not take input from.
errorCodes.turn_unknown: run.resume for a turn the host does not have.
errorCodes.agent_access_denied: The site owner may not use the agent now.
errorCodes.host_frozen: run.rejected: she is moving between her ends; nothing reaches her until the move is done or cancelled.
errorCodes.host_moved: run.rejected: she does not live on this site now.
errorCodes.internal_error: Something failed on the host; trying again later may work.
errorCodes.not_this_device: A runId that is not one this device's turns started.
errorCodes.too_large: A field longer than its limit (playback.observe: upcomingText 7200 bytes, rig 16 KiB; work.recall: query limits.maxTextChars characters).
errorCodes.outfit_unknown: outfit.wear named a set that is not in her wardrobe, or has no rig.
errorCodes.proposal_unknown: proposal.answer named a proposal that is not open: answered already, expired, or not hers to the site owner.
errorCodes.place_unknown: proposal.answer asked to run a proposal where it cannot run: not one of the card's places.
errorCodes.act_off: act.result: the child's switch for the site asking it to act is off.
errorCodes.act_busy: act.result: the child is running another of the host's requests.
errorCodes.act_unavailable: act.result: the child cannot run Work now (it is not set up, or none of its tools may be used). Also why the host cannot send a request: no child that takes act is linked.
errorCodes.act_timeout: An act.request not started by pickupBy, or a run past maxRunMs.
errorCodes.act_cancelled: act.cancel: the owner dismissed the proposal on the site.
errorCodes.act_revoked: The child was removed from the site, or the site has another owner, while its request was open: the proposal failed.

revoked.description: The device was removed from the site, or gave its token back.

owner_changed.description: The site has another owner; this device was the old owner's.

replaced.description: Another connection of this same device took over.

host_moved.description: Her host lease moved her to another end, or the end she lived on was removed; to a device that dialled in as her host and does not hold the lease (at its epoch) any more, that she moved and it lets its copy go. The upgrade is then refused with host_moved, naming where she lives; a child reconnects seldom.

host_frozen.description: She is moving: her host lease is frozen and no end has her. The upgrade is refused with host_frozen until the move is done or cancelled; a child keeps reconnecting with backoff and says she is moving.

host_is_site.description: hello asked for the host role while the site has no host lease (it holds her, or has none).

bad_frame.description: The hello could not be taken: not an envelope, a body without what it needs, or a role or surface this host does not know.

unsupported_protocol.description: hello.protocol is not one this host speaks.

timeout.description: No hello in time, or nothing heard for missedHeartbeats heartbeats.

unavailable.description: The host is stopping or cannot serve the link now.
